original_value: The one‐dimensional (2D) chaotic encryption algorithm has good encryption performance. For its properties, such as the excellent complexity, pseudo‐randomness, and sensitivity to the initial value of the chaotic sequence. However, compared with other methods, its biggest drawback is that the key space is too small. To address these problems, in this study, the authors introduce an improved 2D logistic sine chaotic map (2D‐LSMM). A novel image encryption scheme based on dynamic DNA sequences encryption and improved 2D‐LSMM is presented. The logistic map is used to control the input of the sine map. And the encoding and operation rules of DNA sequences are determined by 2D‐LSMM chaotic sequences. By implementing dynamic DNA sequence encryption, the encryption process becomes more complicated and harder to be attacked. Simulation experimental results and security analysis show that the authors’ encryption scheme not only achieves proper encryption but can also resist different attacks.

result.paraphrase: The one-dimensional (2D) chaotic encryption algorithm offers strong encryption performance thanks to its excellent complexity, pseudo-randomness, and sensitivity to the chaotic sequence’s initial value. Its main weakness, compared with other approaches, is the limited key space. To solve these issues, the authors present an improved 2D logistic sine chaotic map (2D-LSMM). They also propose a new image encryption scheme that combines dynamic DNA sequence encryption with the improved 2D-LSMM. In this design, the logistic map controls the input to the sine map, while 2D-LSMM chaotic sequences determine the encoding and operation rules of the DNA sequences. Dynamic DNA sequence encryption increases the complexity of the process and makes it harder to attack. Simulation results and security analysis indicate that the scheme provides effective encryption and can withstand various attacks.
